## Executive Summary

Nexus is a modular research infrastructure built on three principles derived from the SSCCS paradigm. At its center is the Core Blackboard: a shared graph that every module reads from and writes to through a single interface. There is no fixed pipeline. Modules coordinate indirectly through the Blackboard, not through direct communication.

The Blackboard stores three primitive types. Facts are verified entities, relations, and experimental results. Intents represent gaps, hypotheses, and exploration directions. Hints are governance rules from contract.nex and user feedback. These three types are the only interface between modules.

Any method can attach to the Blackboard. An OODA loop based on the Cairn pattern explores open search spaces. A fixed pipeline reproduces validated research workflows. A Flow-GRPO learning loop reinforces successful paths. Human operators inject Hints directly. Future methods attach the same way. All results converge to the same three primitives.

The Rust core provides the graph storage, Cypher translation, and algorithm implementations. Production-grade crates (petgraph, rusqlite, cyrs, ndarray) are assembled with minimal glue code. Our contribution is the translation and coordination logic, informed by patterns extracted from Memgraph and Grafeo codebases.

1. The Blackboard is the single interface. Every module writes Facts and Intents, reads Facts and Intents, and respects Hints. No module calls another module directly. Communication is indirect through the shared graph.

2. Small composable units. Each crate does one thing well. Modules communicate through the Blackboard, not through message pipes. Contract.nex is the single governance surface.

3. Design by reference, not by dependency. The architecture is informed by Memgraph and Grafeo but depends on neither. We extract their patterns, not their code.

Nexus is itself an instance of the SSCCS paradigm. The Core Blackboard is the Scheme: an immutable coordinate system that every module shares. Intents and Hints are the Field: dynamic constraints that drive exploration. The act of reading the Blackboard, computing, and writing back is the Observation. The resulting Facts are the Projection: the updated state that becomes the input for the next cycle. Nexus implements SSCCS, and SSCCS describes Nexus. This circularity is not a flaw. It is the bootstrap mechanism that makes the system self-consistent.

### Unified Architecture

The architecture has two layers. The Core Blackboard is the logical layer: a shared graph of Fact, Intent, and Hint primitives that every module reads from and writes to through a single interface. The Rust core is the implementation layer: petgraph stores the graph, cyrs translates Cypher queries, and platform bindings expose the core to different deployment targets.

## Design Decisions

### Why Rust Core, Not Docker Containers

The initial Nexus architecture used Docker containers (Memgraph + proxy + LightRAG) orchestrated by shell scripts. We are transitioning to a Rust-native core for five reasons:

| Reason | Impact |
|---|---|
| Single codebase | cargo build produces WASM (CF Worker) or native binary (server) from same source |
| Zero runtime deps | No Docker, no Python, no bolt proxy, wrangler deploy only |
| Cypher for LLMs | Cypher is the graph language with the richest LLM training data. Rust parses it; petgraph executes it |
| Feature-gated profiles | Grafeo-style feature flags: cargo build --features wasm vs native |
| Portable by construction | Core knows nothing about Cloudflare, bindings/ isolates platform code |

### Why Cypher

Cypher is the only graph query language with sufficient LLM training data for reliable code generation. Grafeo supports six languages, Memgraph supports openCypher 9.0. Our cypher/ crate translates Cypher to petgraph traversals using [cyrs](https://github.com/cyrsdb/cyrs) for parsing → Plan IR.

### Reference Implementations

Two production graph databases were analyzed in depth to inform our design. Neither is a dependency; both are pattern references.

#### Memgraph Insights

| Component | Memgraph Pattern | Our Adaptation |
|---|---|---|
| Storage | In-memory LPG + RocksDB WAL | petgraph (in-memory) + rusqlite WAL |
| Vector search | USearch (C++), Single Store Vector Index (85% less memory) | ndarray cosine, embedding stored as node property |
| Community detection | Louvain + Leiden (C++ MAGE) | community-detection crate |
| PageRank | Custom C++ | petgraph built-in |
| MAGE modules | C API isolation (mg_procedure.h) | Rust trait in modules/ crate |
| Atomic GraphRAG | Single Cypher query = search + expand + rank | cypher/translate.rs chains iterator operations |
| Streaming | Kafka/Pulsar → Cypher triggers | Cloudflare Queues → DO method invocation |
| LLM in Cypher | Python MAGE llm.py → CALL | Worker fetch → Workers AI, result as graph node |

#### Grafeo Insights

| Component | Grafeo Pattern | Our Adaptation |
|---|---|---|
| Language translation | 6 query languages → Unified Logical Plan | cyrs Plan IR → petgraph traversal |
| Execution engine | Push-based operators (Scan, Filter, Expand, Join) | Iterator chain (scan → filter → expand → collect) |
| Feature profiles | browser, embedded, server, full | wasm, server, edge |
| WASM bindings | wasm-bindgen + console_error_panic_hook | bindings/cf/ |
| MVCC | Custom Multi-Version Concurrency Control | rusqlite WAL mode + snapshot isolation |
| Indexes | HNSW (vector) + BM25 (text) + B-tree | ndarray (vector) + regex (text) |
| Leapfrog Join | TrieJoin for multi-way intersections | petgraph neighbors() chaining |

## Architecture Stack

The Rust core is assembled from existing crates, not built from scratch. Each crate maps to a specific capability that Memgraph or Grafeo provides internally through different libraries. The value is in the assembly, not the components.

### External Dependencies: Candidates

Where possible, we depend on stable Rust crates rather than implementing from scratch. Rust crate dependencies are permanent.

#### Graph Storage & Query

| Concern | Candidate | Justification | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Graph structure | **petgraph** (0.6) | Standard Rust graph lib, StableGraph, NodeIndex, built-in PageRank and Dijkstra. No reason to reimplement. | Adopted |
| Persistence / WAL | **rusqlite** (0.31) | SQLite bundled mode works on WASM. 40 years of ACID verification. Memgraph uses RocksDB for the same purpose. | Adopted |
| Cypher parsing | **cyrs** | Parses Cypher to typed Plan IR in one step. Grafeo's design (multiple languages → unified IR) confirms this pattern. | Adopted |
| Vector similarity | **ndarray** (0.15) + cosine | Our data volumes do not require HNSW. When they do, USearch has Rust bindings. Memgraph uses USearch internally. | Adopted |

#### Graph Algorithms

| Algorithm | Candidate | Status | Provided By |
|---|---|---|---|
| Louvain community | community-detection crate | Adopted | Pure Rust, petgraph compatible |
| Leiden community | community-detection crate | Adopted | Same crate, variant feature flag |
| PageRank | petgraph::algo::page_rank | Adopted | Built into petgraph |
| Dijkstra / shortest path | petgraph::algo::dijkstra | Adopted | Built into petgraph |
| Betweenness centrality | petgraph + custom | Candidate | Minimal implementation on top of petgraph |
| Cosine similarity | ndarray | Adopted | Used by vector index; no separate crate needed |

#### Platform Bindings

| Target | Candidate | Deploy Command |
|---|---|---|
| Cloudflare Worker | worker crate (worker-rs) | wrangler deploy |
| AWS Lambda | lambda_runtime crate | cargo lambda deploy |
| Native server | axum + clap | cargo run |
| On-chain (blockchain) | (placeholder) | Future decision |

### Design Principle: Implement Strategically, Depend Widely

Where differentiation matters (Cypher-to-petgraph translation, gap detection heuristics, platform bindings), we write code. Where stability matters (graph algorithms, persistence, parsing), we depend on verified Rust crates. The Rust core is the thinnest possible layer that turns a collection of independent crates into a coherent graph analysis platform.

### Rust Core (nexus-core/)

The core is a Cargo workspace with zero platform dependencies.

```text
nexus-core/
├── core/                   ← Graph storage (petgraph + rusqlite WAL)
│   ├── graph/              ← Node, Edge, Property types
│   ├── store/              ← MemoryStore + SqliteStore
│   ├── index/              ← Vector (ndarray) + Text (BM25)
│   └── mvcc.rs             ← Snapshot isolation via rusqlite
├── cypher/                 ← Cypher → Plan IR → petgraph
│   ├── plan.rs             ← cyrs Plan IR types
│   ├── translate.rs        ← Plan → iterator chain
│   └── parser.rs           ← cyrs integration
├── algorithms/             ← Graph algorithms (Memgraph MAGE pattern)
│   ├── community.rs        ← Louvain/Leiden
│   ├── pagerank.rs         ← petgraph built-in
│   └── path.rs             ← Dijkstra, shortest path
├── modules/                ← Analysis modules
│   ├── gap.rs              ← Gap Detector
│   ├── contract.rs         ← contract interpreter
│   └── trait.rs            ← Module trait definition
├── bindings/               ← Platform bindings
│   ├── cf/                 ← worker-rs (wasm-bindgen)
│   ├── server/             ← axum (native)
│   └── onchain/            ← wasm-runtime (placeholder)
└── Cargo.toml              ← Feature-gated profiles
```

### Cypher Translation

The cypher/ crate translates Cypher to petgraph operations using cyrs. Our gap-detector needs only three patterns:

| Cypher Pattern | petgraph Translation |
|---|---|
| `MATCH (c:Concept) WHERE... RETURN c` | node_indices().filter(label).filter(condition) |
| `OPTIONAL MATCH (c)-[r]-() WITH c, count(r) WHERE rc = 0` | neighbors() + count + filter |
| `MATCH (a)-[r1]->(b) MATCH (a)-[r2]->(b) WHERE type != type` | edges() cartesian product + filter |

We do not implement full Cypher. We implement the subset our modules actually need.

### Graph Algorithms

Graph algorithms follow Memgraph's MAGE module pattern: each algorithm is a standalone function that takes a graph reference and returns results.

| Algorithm | Implementation | Memgraph Source |
|---|---|---|
| Louvain | community-detection crate | mage/cpp/community_detection_module/ |
| Leiden | community-detection crate | mage/cpp/leiden_community_detection_module/ |
| PageRank | petgraph::algo::page_rank | mage/cpp/pagerank_module/ |
| Dijkstra | petgraph::algo::dijkstra | mage/cpp/path_module/ |
| Cosine similarity | ndarray | mage/cpp/node_similarity_module/ |

### Analysis Modules

Modules follow Blackboard semantics: read Facts and Hints, emit Intents and new Facts. Every module shares the same graph interface. Internal implementation (Rust native, LLM-driven, heuristic) is invisible to other modules.

| Module | Input | Output | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gap Detector | Fact graph + Cypher queries | Intent (gap) | TS (deployed) → Rust (porting) |
| OODA Loop (Cairn) | Fact + Intent + Hint | Intent (action) | Future (pattern extracted) |
| Hypothesis Generator | Gap Intent + Fact evidence | Intent (hypothesis) | Future |
| Concept Validator | Hypothesis Intent + experiment | Fact (validated/rejected) | Future |
| Entity extraction | Raw document | Fact (entity) | Future |
| Flow-GRPO Planner | Successful Intent histories | Updated Planner weights | Future |

No module calls another module. All communication passes through the Blackboard. The queue layer serializes writes; the Blackboard handles coordination.

### Artifact Storage & Ingestion

R2 (bucket: ssccs-nexus-af) is the single source of truth. The af-sync worker performs incremental sync between R2 and LightRAG via Queue-based processing with drift detection. Already deployed; no change in Rust migration.

### Platform Bindings

| Binding | Crate | Compilation Target |
|---|---|---|
| Cloudflare Worker | bindings/cf/ | wasm32-unknown-unknown |
| Native Server | bindings/server/ | host |
| On-chain (blockchain) | bindings/onchain/ | wasm32-wasi (placeholder) |

### TypeScript Orchestration

| Worker | Role | Calls Rust Via |
|---|---|---|
| af-sync | R2 artifact sync → RAG engines | HTTP (unchanged) |
| module-hub | Gap Detector, module dispatch | DO service binding → nexus-gap.run() |

### Module Communication: Stigmergy Through the Blackboard

Modules do not call each other. Each module reads from the Core Blackboard and writes back to it. Coordination is indirect, inspired by Cairn's stigmergy pattern: agents leave traces in a shared environment, other agents perceive those traces and adapt their behavior.

The Blackboard stores three primitives as node/edge types in the petgraph store. Facts are what the system has learned. Intents are what the system wants to explore. Hints are governance rules and human guidance.

```text
Core Blackboard (shared graph)
    ├── Fact: verified entity, relation, experiment result
    ├── Intent: gap, hypothesis, exploration direction
    └── Hint: contract.nex rule, user feedback

            ↓ read/write (single interface)
    ┌───────┼───────┬───────┬───────┐
    │       │       │       │       │
  OODA    Fixed   Flow-   Human   Future
  Loop    Pipe    GRPO    Hint    Method
(Cairn)  (Gap→   (Learn)  (Inject)
          Hyp→
          Conc)
```

Key principles. Every method converges on the same three primitives regardless of internal complexity. There is no fixed pipeline. The Blackboard's current state determines which module acts next.

## Contract Governance & Future DeSci

Contract.nex defines research rules: evidence thresholds, novelty minimums, report structure, and reward schedules. Every module evaluates contract.nex before writing to the Blackboard. The governance surface is a single file, not distributed across modules.

Future: Token-incentivized research. Contract.nex can execute on a blockchain. Research contributions become automatically verifiable and rewardable:

```text
Contract.nex → Smart contract (blockchain)
    ├── Gap discovery → Token reward
    ├── Hypothesis validation → Staking + reward
    ├── Experiment replication → Replication reward
    └── Concept drift detection → Drift token
```

Every (origin, intent, result) tuple on the Blackboard has a content-addressable hash. This hash serves as a verifiable proof of contribution, recordable on-chain without storing the full payload.

## Architecture Inspirations

### Current Layer (Graph Core)

| Source | Pattern | What We Adopted |
|---|---|---|
| Memgraph (C++, production) | Atomic GraphRAG (single query = search + expand + rank + prompt) | Iterator chain translation in cypher/translate.rs |
| Memgraph | MAGE module isolation (C API, standalone algorithms) | Rust trait isolation in modules/ crate |
| Memgraph | Single Store Vector Index (embedding as node property) | ndarray cosine on petgraph node weights |
| Memgraph | WAL + in-memory dual storage | rusqlite WAL + petgraph memory store |
| Grafeo (Rust, production) | Unified Logical Plan (6 languages → single IR) | cyrs Plan IR → petgraph translation |
| Grafeo | Push-based execution operators | Iterator chain in cypher/translate.rs |
| Grafeo | Feature-gated WASM profiles (browser/embedded/server) | Cargo.toml feature profiles |
| cyrs / cypher-rs ecosystem | Cypher → typed Plan IR | cyrs as primary parser dependency |
| petgraph ecosystem | StableGraph, NodeIndex, built-in PageRank/Dijkstra | Core graph library |

The key architectural insight from Grafeo is that a unified query IR decouples input languages from execution. Future agent modules (Planner, Verifier, Hypothesis Generator) will query the graph through this same IR. They do not need to know whether the backend is petgraph in memory, SQLite on disk, or a remote CF Worker. The query interface is the plug, the core is the socket. Adding a new query language (GQL, SPARQL, or a future agent DSL) requires only a new parser adapter, not a core change.

### Future Layer: Blackboard + Stigmergy

The Blackboard architecture is validated by Cairn, an AI search engine that solved 54 of 54 penetration testing challenges (610 teams, only team to achieve a full clear) with no LLMs, no training, and no prior knowledge. Cairn's core is a 250-line OODA loop that reads from and writes to a shared blackboard of Fact, Intent, and Hint primitives. Modules coordinate indirectly through stigmergy: they leave traces in the shared environment and perceive traces left by others.

This validates the core insight of Nexus. A fixed pipeline (Gap Detector → Hypothesis Generator → Verifier) is one valid module. But it is not the only module. The OODA loop is another. Flow-GRPO learning is another. Human intervention is another. All attach to the same Blackboard through the same interface.

Future research layers will be implemented as Blackboard modules, not as pipeline stages:

| Paradigm | Source | Core Insight | Blackboard Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| In-the-Flow Agentic Optimization | AgentFlow [arXiv:2510.05592](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.05592) | Trainable Planner, Flow-GRPO learning | Reads successful Intent histories, updates Planner weights |
| Hypothesis-Driven Discovery | HypoChainer [arXiv:2507.17209](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2507.17209) | LLMs + KG + humans build hypothesis chains | Writes Hypothesis Intents, reads Fact graph for evidence |
| Contract-Governed Generation | Story2Proposal [arXiv:2601.20833](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.20833) | Shared contract enforces structural obligations | contract.nex evaluated before every Blackboard write |
| Stigmergic Search | Cairn (validated, 54/54) | Indirect coordination through shared traces | Core coordination mechanism; Queue + Blackboard separation |

### Multi-Layered Blackboard Composition

A Blackboard can contain other Blackboards. A Fact at Layer N becomes a Scheme at Layer N+1. An Observation at Layer N+1 becomes a Hint at Layer N. This mirrors the bootstrap recursion: Nexus implements SSCCS, and SSCCS describes Nexus.

| Layer | Role | Content |
|---|---|---|
| Layer 0: Infrastructure | petgraph Graph, GraphLike trait | Physical node and edge storage |
| Layer 1: Domain | Fact / Intent / Hint nodes | Research documents, experiment results, governance rules |
| Layer 2: Meta | Blackboard composition rules | Rules for how Facts at Layer 1 become Schemes at Layer 2 |
| Layer N: Research | Gaps, hypotheses, validations | Domain-specific knowledge exploration |

The Queue layer enforces Stigmergy across layers. A write at any layer is visible to all layers. The type conversion (Fact to Scheme, Observation to Hint) happens at the Queue consumer, not at the write stage.

### Agent Oracle: The Purest Observer

The Agent Oracle is a module that reads from the Blackboard and writes back predictions and simulation results. It has no special privileges. It uses the same Fact / Intent / Hint interface as every other module.

Oracle input: accumulated (origin, intent, result) histories on the Blackboard. Oracle output: new Facts (predicted outcomes) and new Intents (simulation branches to explore). The Oracle does not need direct communication with any other module. It reads the traces left by real-world experiments, market data ingestors, or hardware simulations, and writes its projections back to the same space.

This applies to any domain. Business simulation: Fact = market data, Intent = strategy proposal, Oracle output = projected outcome. Hardware emulation: Fact = RTL trace, Intent = optimization, Oracle output = utilization prediction. The Blackboard does not distinguish between the two. The primitives are the same.

## Strategic Value

- Blackboard is the single interface. Every module reads and writes the same three types. Internal complexity is irrelevant.
- Stigmergy over orchestration. Modules coordinate indirectly through the Blackboard. No module calls another module. No pipeline dependency chain.
- LLM-optional. Cairn proved 54/54 problems without any LLM. LLMs are accelerators, not requirements.
- Iteration over planning. Interface design improves through repeated use, not upfront specification. Virtual responses enable continuous iteration.
- DeSci-ready. Contract.nex enables token-incentivized research. Content-addressable hashes provide verifiable proofs of contribution.
- Portable core. Same Rust codebase compiles for WASM (edge) and native (server). Zero platform lock-in.

## Edge-to-Cloud Portability & AWS Integration

### Principle: Bindings Are Deployment Targets, Not Architectural Commitments

The platform bindings layer (`bindings/`) isolates deployment-specific code. Adding a new deployment target requires only a new binding crate. The core (`nexus-core/`) never changes.

```text
nexus-core/ (Rust, zero deps)
    │
    ├── bindings/cf/       ← Cloudflare Workers (wasm32-unknown-unknown)
    ├── bindings/aws/      ← AWS Lambda + Graviton (aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu)
    ├── bindings/local/    ← Native server (axum, host architecture)
    └── bindings/onchain/      ← Smart contract (wasm32-wasi, placeholder)
```

| Environment | Binding | Hardware | Latency Profile | Best For |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cloudflare Workers | `bindings/cf/` | Edge (300+ locations) | < 50ms cold, sub-ms warm | Real-time queries, API gateway, gap detection on document arrival |
| AWS Lambda (Graviton) | `bindings/aws/` | ARM64 (Graviton3/4) | < 100ms cold, ms warm | Batch analysis, large-scale community detection, model training |
| AWS EC2 / HPC | `bindings/aws/` | x86_64 / GPU | Sub-ms (warm resident) | Hardware simulation, compiler optimization loops, pre-silicon emulation |
| Local / VPS | `bindings/server/` | Any | 0ms | Development, offline research, private data |

### Why This Matters for SSCCS

SSCCS's research agenda spans multiple compute domains that no single platform can satisfy:

| Research Activity | Compute Profile | Optimal Platform |
|---|---|---|
| Document ingestion & entity extraction | I/O-bound, bursty | CF Workers (edge proximity to R2) |
| Knowledge graph query & gap detection | CPU-bound, graph traversal | CF Workers or Lambda |
| Community detection (Louvain/Leiden) | CPU-bound, iterative | Lambda (Graviton, longer timeout) |
| Hypothesis generation (LLM) | Memory-bound, GPU-accelerated | EC2 with GPU or Workers AI |
| Compiler optimization (SSCCS ↔ llvm-project) | CPU-intensive, iterative | EC2 / HPC |
| Hardware emulation (pre-silicon RTL) | CPU + memory intensive, long-running | EC2 / HPC |
| Training (Flow-GRPO for Planner) | GPU-bound, hours-long | SageMaker / EC2 GPU |

### AWS Integrations: Concrete Paths

#### AWS Lambda + Graviton (Immediate)

Rust compiles natively to `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`. The same `nexus-gap` crate that runs as a CF Worker also runs as a Lambda function on Graviton: no code changes.

#### Amazon S3 ↔ R2 Bridge (Data Gravity)

SSCCS documents live in R2. AWS compute can access them via S3-compatible API:

Or migrate hot data to S3 for lower latency from AWS compute, keeping cold data in R2.

#### AWS Nitro Enclaves for Contract Governance

contract.nex verification can run inside an AWS Nitro Enclave for cryptographic attestation: the verification result comes with a signed proof that the contract was executed faithfully, without relying on blockchain.

#### SageMaker for Flow-GRPO Training

The Learning Loop (Layer 4) trains the Planner via Flow-GRPO. Training trajectories collected from CF Workers are stored in R2, then training runs on SageMaker with GPU instances:

```text
CF Workers → R2 (trajectory JSONL)
    ↓
SageMaker Training Job (ml.g5.xlarge)
    ↓ policy update
New Planner checkpoint → R2
    ↓
CF Workers pick up new checkpoint
```

### Future: Hardware Simulation Integration

SSCCS's core research: Segment, Scheme, Field, Observation, Projection: is about rewriting computing's ontology. This extends naturally to hardware:

#### Pre-Silicon Emulation Pipeline

```text
R2 (RTL designs, benchmark configs)
    ↓
EC2 HPC (Graviton4, 64 vCPU, 256GB RAM)
    ↓
nexus-core compiled as native binary
    ├── graph module ingests simulation traces as temporal graphs
    ├── gap detector finds inefficiencies in pipeline utilization
    ├── community detection groups related hardware modules
    └── contract governs which optimizations are valid
    ↓
Findings → R2 → LLM analysis → Compiler patch proposals → llvm-project PRs
```

#### Why Same Core for Hardware Analysis

The gap-detector that today finds orphaned concepts in documentation will tomorrow find underutilized functional units in RTL simulations. Same graph structure, different data:

| Today (Documents) | Tomorrow (Hardware) |
|---|---|
| Node = Concept / Document | Node = Functional Unit / Pipeline Stage |
| Edge = RELATES_TO / APPEARS_IN | Edge = DATA_FLOW / CONTROL_DEPENDENCY |
| Gap = orphaned concept | Gap = idle functional unit |
| Community = topic cluster | Community = co-optimized module group |
| Embedding = text embedding | Embedding = utilization time-series vector |

```{python}
""")
```

This is not "CF or AWS." It is "CF for what CF does best, AWS for what AWS does best, core is the same either way." The meeting-ready narrative is: SSCCS is building a portable graph analysis platform whose deployment surface spans edge-to-cloud, with zero architectural commitment to any single vendor.

### AWS Meeting Talking Points

1. **Portable core.** Same Rust codebase compiles for Graviton, x86, and WASM. Today CF Workers, tomorrow Lambda.

2. **Data gravity.** R2 (S3-compatible) means AWS compute can access SSCCS data with zero migration. S3 migration path exists if needed.

3. **Hardware research alignment.** SSCCS's Segment/Scheme/Field ontology maps directly to hardware pipeline analysis. Graviton + HPC are the natural compute targets.

4. **Contract governance.** `contract.nex` can run in Nitro Enclaves for cryptographic verification of research outputs. No blockchain required for trust; blockchain optional for token incentives.

5. **Training pipeline.** Flow-GRPO training trajectories come from edge workers; training runs on SageMaker. Clean separation of inference (edge) and training (cloud).

6. No lock-in. `bindings/aws/` is a new crate: the core never changes. Same for any future platform.
